description:
For all the solemnity of the B-2 flyover with four F‑22 Raptors and a silent South Lawn drill, the real business of US President Donald Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping last week was narrower than the choreography. author: Victoria Bela
description:
Two giant pandas have arrived in Atlanta to take up residency at the southern US city’s zoo.
The pandas, male Ping Ping and female Fu Shuang, left Chengdu in China’s southwest on Sunday, within days of Chinese President Xi Jinping wrapping up his three-day state visit to the United States.
During the visit, Xi said the pandas would arrive “in a few days”.
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, whose names mean peace and double blessings, arrived at Atlanta International Airport on a chartered flight, state...
title: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang touch down in the US under new loan deal

description:

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Washington’s proposed military bases and expanded defence presence in Greenland will be akin to a “keep out” sign against potential Arctic military cooperation between Beijing and Moscow, according to analysts.
The US, Denmark and Greenland signed a defence deal on Tuesday that allows Washington to build two new military bases on the world’s largest island, while reaffirming Denmark’s sovereignty over it.
The deal – which updates and amends a 1951 defence agreement between Denmark and the US –...
title: Keep out: why Greenland is the US military’s new eyes in the Arctic on China

author: Caroline Lin
description:
While foreign leaders and their families walk the iconic restored sections of the Great Wall around Beijing, the ancient stones of a remote Ming-era stretch of the structure in northern central China have been sacrificed for cheaper dumping of coal-mining waste.
For nearly 20 years, a section of the wall in Ningwu county, Shanxi province, was used as a short cut to dump slag, despite whistle-blowers repeatedly raising the alarm to officials, according to a report by Chinese state broadcaster...
title: Remote section of China’s Great Wall damaged by 20 years of mine waste dumping

author: Carol Yang
description:
US President Donald Trump has sought to play down exchanges with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on Taiwan independence, saying on Saturday that they touched on the subject only briefly.
“We didn’t talk about it too much. Right now, it’s fine. It’s just moving along,” Trump said. “We didn’t spend a lot of time talking about Taiwan. He understands very much how I feel.”
During the summit in Washington last week, Xi pressed Trump to take an explicit position against Taiwan independence – a...
title: ‘Right now, it’s fine’: Trump brushes off questions about summit talk on Taiwan

author: Shi Jiangtao,Fan Chen
description:
Southeast Asia is welcoming the thaw in US-China ties continuing after the Xi-Trump summit, with analysts saying the region could feel less pressure alongside fewer open frictions between the two over the South China Sea.
Yet, caution persists as the summit left deeper disputes unresolved.

title: Why Southeast Asia feels relief and caution after the Xi-Trump summit

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
Mrima Hill, a sacred site about 65km (40 miles) southwest of Mombasa on Kenya’s Indian Ocean coast, is emerging as a new front in the US-China rivalry for critical minerals.
US-led and Chinese bidders are competing for rights to develop the site, which is rich in rare earths and niobium, a metal used to make steel stronger and lighter.

title: How Kenya’s sacred Mrima Hill became new front in US-China minerals rivalry
